workflow-doc.title: Beads graph classification and citation sweep

banner.read-when: auditing or normalizing every bead, its title, type, labels, dependencies, redundancy, or research citations
banner.note: This is a graph-wide maintenance procedure. It refines the standing tracker rules; it does not relax backup, synchronization, field-safety, or owner-controlled status policy.

section.title: Define the mutation contract
section.prose: Write the allowed change dimensions before reading the graph. Treat every omitted dimension as immutable. A classification sweep normally permits titles, types, and labels; status, priority, ownership, dependency edges, and standing text fields remain unchanged unless the owner names them explicitly.

list.item: Enumerate every issue, including closed and deferred issues. Record the expected issue count and partition the complete ID set into disjoint audit batches.
Load the complete label and type vocabularies before classifying anything. The vocabulary is data, not an assumed convention.
Load the closed commitlint scope vocabulary. Titles follow the tracker title schema, including lexically sorted multi-scope prefixes.
Separate classification evidence, redundancy evidence, and citation evidence. Similar words or labels are not proof that two beads have the same contract.

section.title: Synchronize, back up, and capture a baseline
section.prose: Pull before relying on tracker reads. Create and sync a Dolt-native backup outside the project tree before the first graph mutation. Keep that backup configured and available until post-mutation verification and remote synchronization succeed.
section.code: bd dolt pull bd label list-all --json bd types list-all --json bd backup init /durable/path/beads-backup-YYYY-MM-DD bd backup sync bd backup status --json bd export -o /durable/path/beads-preupdate-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl

list.item: Record issue and status counts, the type distribution, label assignments, dependency edges, comments, and hashes or normalized snapshots of every field declared immutable.
Record the backup locator, last Dolt commit, database size, and successful sync time in the sweep report.
Workers may inspect disjoint batches in parallel, but the classification phase is read-only. One coordinator owns the mutation plan and later database writes.

section.title: Audit every bead in read-only passes

row.cell: Does the title identify the outcome under the smallest accurate scope set?
Full contract, case-sensitive literals, and the closed scope vocabulary.
Which one work type describes the bead's actual deliverable?
Description, acceptance criteria, current lifecycle role, and child structure.
Would every expected exact-label search retrieve this bead?
Complete label families from list-all; use a new category only when no existing label surfaces the bead precisely.
Can a contributor reconstruct and execute the complete task from this bead plus standing guidance alone?
Outcome, boundaries and non-goals, decisions and provenance, affected interfaces, dependencies, acceptance and verification, and authoritative references.
Do two beads own the same executable contract, rather than adjacent or historical work?
Full standing fields, comments, status, dependencies, dependents, chronology, and deliverables for every candidate.
Does every research-bearing claim retain an identifiable source?
Local register, project provenance, and primary-source landing metadata; unresolved shorthand stays explicitly uncertain.

list.item: Each worker returns every assigned ID exactly once, including explicit no-change decisions. The coordinator rejects missing IDs, duplicate IDs, invalid types, unknown labels, and title scopes outside the closed vocabulary.

Never act from title or label similarity alone. Re-read each candidate's complete live record immediately before proposing a merge, and prefer a dependency or related edge when contracts are distinct but provenance is shared.

Resolve shorthand from surrounding bead context and local provenance first, then verify the candidate against a primary source. Mark inference and confidence. Do not turn a thematic similarity into a definitive citation.

section.title: Build and review one deterministic mutation plan
section.prose: Materialize one machine-readable plan keyed by bead ID. For every field, record before value, after value, rationale, and evidence. New labels and dependency changes are separate explicit inventories. Citation additions carry the complete replacement for the bead's compact standing references section; research references are the sole exception to the comment-only update rule.

list.item: The plan's ID set equals the baseline ID set for a full sweep. Every status is byte-for-byte preserved unless status was explicitly authorized. Every non-target standing field and graph edge is preserved.
Present uncertain citation candidates, genuinely new taxonomy categories, destructive redundancy remedies, and status changes for owner adjudication before applying them.
Update existing beads through the bead update, label, comment, and dependency interfaces. Do not import an exported graph as an upsert plan.

section.title: Apply a short, single-writer mutation batch
section.prose: Refresh the backup immediately before the first write. Use one coordinator and deterministic ID order. Apply metadata corrections first, dependency changes second, and standing citation updates last. Stop on the first failed command; do not treat emitted JSON as success without checking the command result and the live bead.

list.item: Run backup sync and status again, then confirm the baseline issue and status counts still match.
Apply each planned title, type, and label update without touching status or standing text.
Apply only owner-approved redundancy edges or consolidations. Regenerate the passive export after dependency changes.

Add complete, deduplicated citations directly to the bead's compact standing references section. Preserve owner-approved uncertainty in the reference annotation; do not leave the canonical bibliography only in comments.
Commit the tracker working set once the bounded batch succeeds, then push the Dolt state before any downstream process relies on it.

section.title: Verify conservation and intended change
section.code: bd export -o /durable/path/beads-postupdate-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl bd dolt commit -m 'normalize bead graph metadata' bd dolt push bd backup status --json

list.item: Compare baseline and final exports by ID. Assert exact expected title, type, label, comment, and approved-edge changes. Assert every status and every untargeted field or edge is unchanged.
Re-enumerate all labels and types; validate every title scope, lexical ordering, case posture, and length; verify issue and status counts; confirm no issue vanished or appeared unexpectedly.
Verify every accepted citation exists exactly once in the bead's standing body and includes identifying metadata and a resolvable locator. List remaining ambiguity rather than silently dropping it.
Inspect each altered candidate pair again in live tracker state. Confirm the surviving contracts and graph links match the approved remedy.
Run the documentation-class gate and formatter check for this workflow document, then the repository merge gate before landing tracked guidance.

section.title: Record the audit and retire temporary state
section.prose: Write the detailed sweep report in the external notes repository. It records the contract, baseline, complete structural change inventory, new taxonomy, citation decisions and unresolved candidates, redundancy decisions, backup proof, synchronization evidence, and verification results.

list.item: Distill standing rules into tracker guidance and keep contributor-specific paths, batch artifacts, and session mechanics out of tracked history.
Remove pre/post exports and generated mutation plans after the report contains their durable conclusions.
After successful verification and synchronization, unregister the backup configuration. Delete retained backup data only when the owner authorizes that destructive cleanup.
Report every new or changed metadata category, every residual ambiguity, every rejected remedy, and the exact commands that proved the final graph.
